tips.title: Tips
tips.subtitle: Drawn from what the weather is doing right now

pressureFalling.title: Fish the edge of the drop-off
pressureFalling.body: On falling pressure predators leave the holes and sit at two to three metres. Work the lure along the ledge, not across the bottom of the pit.

pressureRising.title: Go deeper and slow down
pressureRising.body: Rising pressure pins fish to the bottom. Work the holes, use long pauses and a smaller lure.

pressureSteady.title: Steady barometer, steady tactics
pressureSteady.body: With the pressure flat fish hold their usual spots. Start with proven marks and resist swapping lures too early.

windRipple.title: Stand so the wind hits the bank
windRipple.body: The chop pushes food to the leeward bank — baitfish follow, and predators follow them. Mirror-flat water is worse right now.

windStrong.title: Get behind a headland
windStrong.body: In strong wind look for sheltered bays and leeward points. A heavier lure keeps contact with the bottom.

windCalm.title: Finer and quieter
windCalm.body: In dead calm fish see everything. Thinner fluorocarbon, a smaller lure, a longer cast — and no banging around the boat.

waterWarming.title: Speed the retrieve up
waterWarming.body: Fish are no longer sluggish: pause two or three seconds instead of five, shorten the jerk. Warm water suits a 3″ twister and a minnow.

waterCooling.title: Slow everything down
waterCooling.body: Cooling water slows the metabolism. Long pauses, a smaller lure, and fish the deepest stretches.

waterSteady.title: Keep the usual rhythm
waterSteady.body: Water temperature is stable, so fish are not relocating. Revisit the same marks at different hours.

waterUnknown.title: Read the air instead
waterUnknown.body: There is no water reading — estimate it from the recent average air temperature and do not trust the forecast too precisely.

cloudBroken.title: Go bright and noisy
cloudBroken.body: In murky light fish key on contrast and vibration. Acid colours and wide-action lures beat natural ones.

cloudOvercast.title: Predators have spread over the shallows
cloudOvercast.body: Under full cloud fish are not afraid of open water. Cover the shallows and the mouth of the bay.

cloudClear.title: Look for shade and depth
cloudClear.body: In bright sun fish sit under snags, in bank shade and deep. Fish early, late, or in the shadows.

moonNew.title: Do not miss the morning window
moonNew.body: On a new moon the strongest phase is the first two hours after sunrise. Be on the water early, not at eight.

moonFull.title: A full moon shifts the bite to the night
moonFull.body: On a full moon fish feed at night and are sluggish in the morning. Plan a late evening or a very early start.

precipitationDrizzle.title: Drizzle is no reason to go home
precipitationDrizzle.body: Light rain knocks down surface glare and adds oxygen. The bite dies before a thunderstorm, not under drizzle.

precipitationHeavy.title: Sit the downpour out
precipitationHeavy.body: Heavy rain clouds the water and kills the bite. Wait for it to ease and fish the first hours after.

precipitationDry.title: In dry weather, work the clock
precipitationDry.body: With no rain the bite holds at dawn and dusk. In the middle of the day pick shade and depth.

timeDawn.title: The morning window is open
timeDawn.body: The most active hour of the day has already started. Do not spend it rigging up.

timeDusk.title: The evening session has begun
timeDusk.body: The last two hours of light are the day's second window. Take your best mark right now.

timeDay.title: Fish spots, not water
timeDay.body: Between the windows fish hold still. Work cover — snags, ledges, bank shade — instead of searching wide.

airWaterWarmer.title: The shallows have warmed — fish are there
airWaterWarmer.body: Air warmer than water means shallow ground heats fastest. Start there.

airWaterColder.title: A cold snap drives fish deep
airWaterColder.body: Air colder than water cools the shallows first. Work the holes and the drop-offs.

diary.title: Journal
diary.subtitle: Log your catches and the stats on your profile start counting your own fish.
diary.emptyBody: The first entry takes half a minute: date, fish, weight and place. A note about tackle or bait will pay off next season.

about.title: About
about.disclaimer: The bite index is an estimate based on open weather data. It is not a guarantee of a catch.
about.sources: Weather data and settlement search: Open-Meteo. Maps: OpenFreeMap, built on OpenStreetMap; OpenStreetMap tiles in the browser and offline. Map tiles for your spots are stored on the device. The moon phase is computed on the device using Meeus algorithm.
about.rules: Rules, closed seasons and licence requirements vary by region. Check local regulations before you go.
about.privacy: No accounts, analytics or ads. Your journal, photos, profile and saved places stay on this phone. To fetch the forecast, coordinates rounded to about 1 km are sent to Open-Meteo; the map comes from OpenFreeMap and OpenStreetMap, place names from your phone's geocoder. See the privacy policy for details.
